body:
Bill Cotton, a North Dakota farmer long known for stepping up when his neighbors needed help, was diagnosed with stage 4 brain cancer. Within days, the community's response was overwhelming: around 70 to 80 trucks and multiple harvesters arrived to support him in return.

The gathering represented far more than a practical response to harvest season. Cotton's years of quiet generosity—showing up when others faced hardship—had built a network of genuine reciprocal care. In his moment of crisis, his neighbors didn't hesitate to repay the countless times he had been there for them.

The scene of dozens of vehicles converging on his farm was a powerful reminder of how rural communities function at their best: built on trust, mutual aid, and the understanding that help given is never truly lost.
